text:
toni: noticed a weird spike in the console active-streams graph during the canary. counts doubled but user traffic is steady. attached screenshots (not pasted).
ashok: can you paste proxy logs around that minute? sounds like session id churn / fingerprint flip.
toni: here are the relevant lines:
```
[proxy] 03:14:02 NEW_CONN uid=client-42 fingerprint=0000a1
[proxy] 03:14:03 CLOSE uid=client-42 reason=keepalive_timeout
[proxy] 03:14:03 NEW_CONN uid=client-42 fingerprint=0000b2
[proxy] 03:14:04 NEW_CONN uid=client-42 fingerprint=0000c3
```
seems like fingerprint changes on reconnect.
claire: could be the LB rewriting source or the client switching network. our fingerprint currently = hash(ip + user-agent). :face_with_monocle:
sam: idea: prefer a client-supplied X-Session-Fingerprint header when present, fallback to ip+ua. but that affects quota attribution and routing keys.
toni: big problem: console and billing currently count on connection creations. churn -> double billing events for same logical session. do we pause canary?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused at 60% because streaming.sessions.created > 2x baseline for 1m window
emily: we need better telemetry first: emit session.change_reason and session.fingerprint fields in logs/metrics. also add a metric for stream.session.reused so console can show real concurrency vs conn_count.
ashok: i can do a small runtime PR to emit stream.session.reused and tag new_conn events with fingerprint_before/after. also add a per-tenant metric so we can filter noisy tenants.
claire: also change dashboard queries: use unique fingerprint counts (distinct_count(fingerprint)) instead of conn_count in the SLO panel, otherwise ops will be paged for normal client reconnects.
toni: will switching to client-provided fingerprint break sticky routing between proxies/shards?
sam: sticky routing uses hash(fingerprint) % shard_count. if we accept client header we must validate entropy and length. untrusted values could cause hotshard collisions. propose signing/normalize step in front of router.
emily: runtime could emit a normalized header 'fingerprint-v' after validation; route by that. console can show both original and normalized for auditing.
toni: plan: ashok PR to add metrics/log tags, sam implements validation+normalization, emily updates dashboard to distinct fingerprint, i'll hold canary until metrics show session.reused ~ previous baseline. thanks all :thumbsup:
